name: eliminate each variable below its pivot, then back-substitute
mechanism: for each column in turn, subtract multiples of the pivot row from the rows below so that column is zero beneath the pivot; the system becomes triangular and is solved from the last variable upward

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Gaussian elimination' in section Computational mathematics / Numerical algorithms / Linear algebra:
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Gauss–Jordan elimination': solves systems of linear equations
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Tridiagonal matrix algorithm (Thomas algorithm)': solves systems of tridiagonal equations

requires: a nonzero pivot (row swaps supply one)
fails_when: small pivots amplify rounding; cubic cost; fill-in destroys sparsity
